description: Partitioned finite workflow coordination. This schema owns the live owner protocol. Complete Workflow records are shared inspection projections; they are not replicated participant state or live mutation inputs.

InputReference.description: workflow.journal.submit carries a content-staged canonical JournalCommand under exact receiving owner, workflow scope, current principal, digest and byte length. Replies are immutable typed record references, read through bounded record.read chunks with current scope authorization on every read. Lost replies rediscover the original request outcome by ID. Upload and download interruption retain complete extent and resume offsets; frame/page limits do not cap total owners, children, material or history. Request-selected schema readers or trust keys are forbidden. The bounded submit reference carries exact workflow_id and command_id. After current read authorization, an indexed accepted command whose immutable command digest equals input.digest returns its original record reference before any staged-byte read or admission freshness check. Changed digest under that identity conflicts. New inputs must decode to the same workflow_id/command_id; wire identities alone never create an accepted command. Exact retained replay survives expiry or loss of the original unpinned staging copy.

ListRequest.description: Start or resume a stable permission-filtered traversal of local workflow discovery anchors. Each anchor is the original retained initialization reference; workflow.journal.events discovers all later events. Current disclosure permission is checked per workflow on every page. A page may be empty while next_cursor is non-null. A process restart explicitly expires old cursors; a fresh traversal rediscovers complete durable custody.

Reservation.description: A current observation is not a lease. Native conditions required by an installed phase must be protected by owner-held reservations, exclusions or fencing through the corresponding effects. The owner acquires and durably records that protection before voting, checks its exact generation and current permission at local admission, and refuses admission when protection cannot be maintained. Expiry, timeout, restart, a certificate or an exact retry neither renews protection nor releases a hold. Release and abort require positively established owner-native conditions. Lost protection closes new admission and preserves uncertainty and accepted work for reconciliation.

Command.description: One exact caller identity and closed action-specific input. The independently selected receiving owner chooses gate/member context, installed signing keys, gate enrollment, permissions and native services. These are never supplied by payload fields. gate.create stages the complete proposal exactly once at its gate; member.join stages only the approved signed local projection.

JournalRecord.description: An immutable original signed journal outcome. Ed25519 signs the UTF-8 bytes fishhat/workflow-journal/v1 followed by a NUL byte and the canonical JSON of every field except signature. Verification selects a key from independently installed owner-epoch trust and exact gate enrollment. A supplied key_id never enrolls a key. body.command_digest commits the exact original JournalCommand, including action and request ID; replay returns this original outcome without new attribution or timestamps.

payload.description: Commitment to canonical bytes of the exact complete original signed projection record, including its signature. The recovering owner obtains those bytes, the original schema closure and qualified reader solely from independently approved OriginRecoveryContext custody; no historical body, trust key, schema or reader is supplied by this command. The digest must equal that exact trusted retained projection. Ordinary member.join remains a current-schema admission of its complete projection.

AbandonmentFacts.description: Positive native facts for the exact UNUSED successor, never a statement that uncertain original work stopped. The native owner permanently tombstones successor admission and preserves every original outcome, hold and retired admission. An absent journal, timeout, expiry or unreachable actor does not establish these facts.

AcceptedInput.description: Immutable accepted input custody, discovered from an outcome without saved driver input IDs. The command_id is the acceptance record id, workflow_id is its protected workflow resource, and all owners equal the receiver. Input purpose is workflow-input and binding is workflow-journal with that exact command and workflow. Read complete bytes through content.get; verify digest/size against the handle and digest against the original signed acceptance body.command_digest before interpreting the exact original Command. The receiver indexes complete canonical input once on durable append or cold restore. Lookup and every chunk reauthorize current local disclosure; possession grants no admission. Historical owner epochs use separately qualified historical readers and explicit custody recovery.

ProtocolRules.description: Normative authority, custody, concurrency, recovery and aggregate work rules for the live workflow journal protocol. This installed-only dependency is part of every rooted journal schema identity; it is not a caller-provided authority object.

const.authority: A workflow has one finite owner-held gate journal and one local journal at each participating owner. The driver is a caller, never the gate authority. Each owner independently approves the exact gate owner epoch, signing key, workflow manifest, local projection and scope before preparation. A request, certificate, key supplied by its sender, client cache or optional reporting service cannot enroll that delegation. The delegation permits the gate to verify complete shared barriers; it never permits it to authorize another owner's Plan, fabricate native observations, release another owner's holds or execute a foreign resource. Gate custody and signing are native owner responsibilities, not a permanent management service.
const.partition: The gate validates the complete immutable WorkflowProposal once and partitions it once by owner. It retains the complete proposal, owner index, installed requirements, dependency closure and signed local projections. A member retains its exact local participants, reviewed Plans, continuation intentions, required local material and explicit dependency references, plus a constant-size common header. A member is never required to fetch, retain, rehash or verify the full peer roster, peer Plans, all-owner proof vector or global recovery manifest. Shared bytes and native material needed by multiple declared consumers are accounted for separately. No owner or collection count limit is introduced.
const.agreement: Each member durably retains and independently authorizes its exact local projection, driver and gate delegation, then signs one preparation for the exact common manifest and local projection digest. The gate accepts exactly one authenticated preparation for each indexed owner. Duplicates cannot replace missing owners. It commits agreement only after the entire installed closure is present; local preparation alone permits no child effects. All native-role participants, including a relocation destination without an ordinary child, remain required.
const.rounds: A round binds the workflow, manifest, installed procedure and requirement identities, gate epoch, adjacent from/to phases, authority and one common round identity. A driver-authority round binds the current driver term. A native-owner round and its decision use null driver_term and can only settle or refresh the final adjacent barrier; each local command still selects that receiver's current retained generation and term. Native settlement preserves mixed terms during partial transfer, cannot admit a new child or advance an intermediate phase, and does not activate a transfer. Issuers sign the same common round once; receiver advance IDs and capsule generations are absent from its subject. Each member vote binds its exact local projection, local generation, child outcomes, native evidence and durable reservation. The gate verifies every indexed owner once and commits a decision only after exact complete coverage. It retains an indexed source for every round, preserving the original round, issuer votes, committed decision and member certificates across later rounds, transfer activation and native settlement. Certificate requests select an exact round_id and owner; each member has one immutable certificate per committed round, and a changed request identity cannot replace that certificate. An ordinary next or refresh round cannot replace a committed current round until all member certificates have been durably minted. Delivery acknowledgments are unnecessary: lost delivery rediscovers the original immutable certificate through bounded journal discovery. An uncommitted current round requires its exact supersedes identity before replacement and cannot acquire a decision afterward. Native terminal settlement can establish a fresh terminal round while preserving every prior committed certificate source. Materializing a certificate for an already committed round preserves that original decision and supplies no renewed protection. Members verify the approved gate signature, exact common round and their own retained reservation and local state; current local permission, term, lifecycle, expiry and actual native protection govern application and effects. Members never receive an all-owner proof bundle.
const.native_protection: A current observation is not a lease. Native conditions required by an installed phase must be protected by owner-held reservations, exclusions or fencing through the corresponding effects. The owner acquires and durably records that protection before voting, checks its exact generation and current permission at local admission, and refuses admission when protection cannot be maintained. Expiry, timeout, restart, a certificate or an exact retry neither renews protection nor releases a hold. Release and abort require positively established owner-native conditions. Lost protection closes new admission and preserves uncertainty and accepted work for reconciliation. The native primitive must maintain the promised protection across owner process failure or fence every dependent effect boundary closed. It cannot revoke unilaterally while a dependent admission remains possible. If the installed backend cannot provide that guarantee, preparation/reservation refuses; polling, expiry, notifications and signed observations are not substitutes. Controlled release first closes dependent admissions and positively settles the relevant accepted obligations. The protection discriminator names this required primitive; merely asserting its spelling in JSON never supplies it.
const.children: Every child remains bound to the exact local reviewed Plan, owner epoch, resource, request ID, workflow membership, phase, material custody, approved adapter/runtime selection and installed continuation lineage. Gate certificates do not replace current Plan review, native permission or normal Operation admission. Known-success barriers require exact retained succeeded Operations with known effects and the correct result/Plan/workflow identities. Failed, unknown, unrelated-workflow or unaccepted work cannot count as success. Local child acceptance and immutable outcome custody precede acknowledgement. Completed recovery slots are nonexecutable.
const.journal: Owners serialize admission and append immutable request/outcome events before acknowledgement. Opening requires explicit initialization for a genuinely new journal; missing, wrong-epoch, wrong-schema, corrupt or truncated accepted custody is never treated as an empty owner. An exact retained request ID is resolved from a protected index before freshness checks; identical input returns its original outcome and attribution after current read authorization. Changed input conflicts. Ordinary admission processes only new local bytes and exact indexed dependencies; it does not reserialize a whole manifest or rescan all retained events. Cold restore reads and validates the complete journal once to rebuild indexes. An explicit complete audit inspection may materialize a shared Workflow view; such a view is not a member admission input or a required per-event rewrite.
const.transfer: A driver transfer has one common gate-owned proposal. Each member durably freezes its own old-term admission once and signs its exact freeze. The gate verifies all freezes once before committing the new term. Each member installs that term only against its own retained freeze and independently approved new driver. New work remains closed until the gate has the complete installation closure and each admitting member has the matching activation decision. Partial transfer cannot reopen old admission, admit under a partially installed new term, change gate authority or manufacture missing evidence. Already accepted native work may settle under owner authority independently of transfer, without admitting new children or completing the transfer.
const.recovery: The gate owns one complete recovery manifest; each member retains only its exact local recovery projection and custody dependencies. Original admissions are durably retired and one successor is exclusively reserved before successor execution. A different successor requires positive, verified abandonment of the prior unused reservation. Missing or unreachable custody, timeout, expiry and an empty restored journal are not evidence of never-prepared, unaccepted, stopped or successful work. Positive local disposition evidence preserves exact known completed Operations, explicit unknown effects, holds, material and original schema identities. Uncertainty blocks redispatch until native recovery establishes a safe disposition. Missing gate custody blocks new shared admissions while local accepted work remains independently inspectable and settleable. Gate restoration or replacement requires qualified exact authoritative custody and explicit owner approval; local snapshots cannot invent a missing shared head. Before replacing an uncommitted unused successor, the gate first records an abandonment proposal that closes recovery commitment. Each local owner then positively proves that exact successor unused and permanently tombstoned. Only complete all-owner abandonment permits a gate certificate and a new successor reservation; each local owner must observe that certificate before replacement. The original remains retired and its uncertain/completed effects do not change. A known accepted original Operation can never become unaccepted through reconciliation: per-child updates bind the exact prior disposition and original Operation to a separate successful typed recovery Operation and Plan. Completed and positive-unaccepted facts remain immutable. A current-epoch recovery-only member initializes through member.recover using only the digest of the exact complete originally signed projection. The original projection bytes and qualified historical schema reader come from independently approved native custody context. A historically valid projection is never forced through the current closed projection body schema or accepted on a caller-chosen reader. Digest substitution conflicts, and this recovery-only actor cannot admit ordinary children.
const.transport: workflow.journal.submit carries a content-staged canonical JournalCommand under exact receiving owner, workflow scope, current principal, digest and byte length. Replies are immutable typed record references, read through bounded record.read chunks with current scope authorization on every read. Lost replies rediscover the original request outcome by ID. Upload and download interruption retain complete extent and resume offsets; frame/page limits do not cap total owners, children, material or history. Request-selected schema readers or trust keys are forbidden. The bounded submit reference carries exact workflow_id and command_id. After current read authorization, an indexed accepted command whose immutable command digest equals input.digest returns its original record reference before any staged-byte read or admission freshness check. Changed digest under that identity conflicts. New inputs must decode to the same workflow_id/command_id; wire identities alone never create an accepted command. Exact retained replay survives expiry or loss of the original unpinned staging copy.
const.growth: For an entire execution including initialization, preparation, all installed phases, child binds and outcomes, driver transfer, successor recovery, durable writes, cold restoration, pages and exact retries, required work is O(B + N + E + Q + H + R + S). B is the unique logical manifest and local intent/material input bytes, counted before protocol replication; N is distinct owners; E is actual declared dependency delivery extent; Q is required owner-phase participation; H is newly accepted history bytes; R is actual retry bytes. Material genuinely required at N native consumers has N consumer incidences. Gratuitous protocol copies and all-to-all messages cannot inflate these denominators. All transmitted, canonicalized, hashed, signed, verified, stored, rewritten, read and parsed bytes across all participants count. Per-owner linear checks, precomputed setup, caches and fixed owner counts do not establish this aggregate bound. H counts each logical accepted input/outcome once per semantic event, not copies, expanded proof delivery or whole-history rewrites. R is the declared retry schedule and logically selected retry payload, not permission to absorb repeated whole-resource work into a larger denominator. Increasing owner, local child, material and retry axes are measured separately; a prescribed fixed-phase complete workload must also demonstrate O(B + N + E) growth without using generated storage as input extent. S is the complete authoritative byte input to independently required cold restorations. Each such restoration validates each retained byte once. Ordinary admissions and retries cannot invoke a whole-history rebuild or charge it to S. The fixed-restore-schedule aggregate proof includes every actual restore read, parse and reconstruction; it does not promise a restart-count-independent cost when an external failure schedule repeatedly requires rereading growing authoritative history. A stronger bound across arbitrary process restarts requires a separately qualified persistent trusted index and is not established by this reference model.
const.discovery: workflow.journal.list discovers authorized local workflow heads without caller state. Each reference scopes its workflow ID. workflow.journal.events then enumerates every retained immutable event reference for that exact owner/workflow, including initialization, local projection/gate route, accepted bindings, permits, outcomes, transfer and recovery. A cursor pins one stable high-water event boundary and exact scope; appending later work cannot replace its members or restart a prefix. Pages contain at most 64 references but have no total-count limit. Current permission is checked on every page and chunk. The reference delivery model explicitly expires its cursors on owner-process restart; a fresh traversal rediscovers all durable events without deleting, rebinding or silently omitting custody. workflow.journal.input then content.get makes the exact original accepted command retrievable for every event, including shared gate proposals and collected owner votes. Each selected complete input is returned once during complete inspection; bounded retries do not reserialize full history.
